title: A diagnosis at three
first: A three-year-old boy in a village in Madhya Pradesh was losing strength in his muscles. His family, a long way from any specialist hospital, took it for poor nutrition. An NGO working in the area arranged a molecular test, and the result was Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
rest: With a diagnosis at three, the family could begin supportive therapy and join a patient support group, instead of spending years without an answer.

title: Two carriers, one plan
first: A couple in Chhattisgarh had lost their first child to spinal muscular atrophy without ever learning the cause. During their second pregnancy they were referred to us through a government screening programme. Carrier testing showed that both parents carry the SMA mutation.
rest: With counselling and early testing they could plan with full information. They now have a healthy child.

title: What had been called fate
first: In a village in Odisha, a young couple had watched two children in their extended family live with severe anaemia and repeated infections. Testing showed that both of them carry the sickle cell gene.
rest: In their village the illness had been put down to fate. The couple now know what it is, how it is passed on and what their choices are.
